newsitem.title: USA: Tosco traces cause of fatal Jan. blast.
newsitem.headline: Tosco traces cause of fatal Jan. blast.

text.p: Tosco Corp said on Thursday that a fatal January explosion and fire at the company's Avon Refinery in California was caused by a high temperature increase that led to a pipe rupture.
The fire on January 21 killed one person and injured 25 more at the hydrocracker unit, which converts heavier oils into gasoline and diesel products, Tosco said.

The cause of the rapid increase in temperature in the pipe could not be conclusively determined, Tosco said in a statement. It said the incident was "highly unprecedented in the 34-year history of the hydrocraker unit."
A contributing cause of the incident was that the unit was not depressured in response to the temperature increase, Tosco said.
The incident happened so rapidly -- in a seven and a half minute span -- that it was unlike anything the refinery's operators had previously experienced, Tosco said.
Operators had questioned whether the temperature indications shown on certain control room instruments were accurate, because of previous computer malfunctions with similar instruments, Tosco said.
During the investigation, Tosco said it found that none of the instruments malfunctioned that night.
Tosco said it issued the report to authorities and will present detailed findings in Martinez, Calif., on June 3.
Tosco said it will implement a series of corrective actions that will prevent such an incident from recurring, including upgrading controls and improving its emergency response access.
